habits.habits: All three are white with a thin top nav. Each hero stacks a large headline, a gray paragraph, a filled button beside a text link and a small line of trust notes, with a framed product mockup cropped below. The same two-tone green and black appear on every site, the mockups use the same hairline-divided tables and progress bars, and the sample data (time zones, budget categories) repeats. Only the typefaces differ: Korean sans, serif and wide grotesk.

All three are white with black or teal pill buttons and the same pattern of headline, paragraph, button, text link and gray notes. Each product preview is a bordered data table with a heavy top rule, a hairline row grid and one red warning value. Spacing is the same and the color is mostly black and white throughout. The only variety is in the type (serif Korean, extended grotesk, serif) and in centered versus split alignment.

Two of the three sites (Tandem and Moa) share a gray background, a split hero with a paper-receipt card and a red rubber-stamp gimmick, plus monospace numbers. All three use the same pair of buttons (black filled and outlined) and the same small line of trust notes. Pennywise breaks the pattern with a colorful bento grid, but the receipt-and-stamp idea is repeated across clients.

The backgrounds differ (deep green band, cream and white), but the layout underneath is the same: headline, paragraph, a filled button plus an underlined link, small notes, then a wide product card with a left summary figure, hairline rows and one red 'over' or 'blocked' value. Tandem's timeline with green bars echoes the green progress bars on Pennywise and Moa. Moa's centered hero with a dashboard below differs a little.

The palettes are clearly distinct (cobalt with yellow, dark mode with mint, sage with a red CTA) and the compositions vary: mockup on the left, full-width table below, card on the right. Display faces also differ (serif, heavy grotesk, heavy Korean). What still repeats is the tidy product card with hairline rows and one red accent value, the microcopy line under the buttons, and the paired filled and outlined buttons.

Each site has its own background color (royal blue, sage, near-black) and its own type voice (serif, heavy Korean display, tight grotesk). What repeats is the hero structure: a big headline with a product card beside or below it, a pair of buttons (filled primary and outlined 'See how it works'), a small gray line of reassurances under the buttons, and a fake UI card filled with realistic data (timestamps, amounts, progress bars). The trusted-by logo line looks the same as in other sets.

Every hero is a big headline over or beside one wide product card in a rounded panel. Each uses a filled primary button with a text-link secondary and a gray reassurance line under the CTAs. Green is the accent on two of the three sites. Data rows are label on the left and amount on the right with thin dividers, and there are small progress bars. Hero widths and spacing are similar. The background treatments do differ (white, a full-bleed dark green band, beige).

The receipt/paper-slip idea appears twice (Tandem digest, Moa fee receipt), with a torn zigzag edge and a red circular rubber stamp ('DECIDED', '수수료 0원'). The backgrounds are a similar light gray. All three pair a black filled button with an outlined secondary, add a gray reassurance line, and use monospace-style numbers set right. Pennywise's colorful bento cards break the pattern, but the other two are clearly one idea used twice.

All three are white with no color: black pill buttons, gray text, and an underlined text-link secondary. Each puts a thin-ruled, bordered data table or panel under the headline with hairline row dividers and figures set right. Every site has an editorial display face (serif on Pennywise and Moa, extended grotesk on Tandem). The nav, the reassurance microcopy and the table chrome are the same on every site. Only the headline alignment changes (left, centered, split).

All three are white with a headline, then CTAs, then a large bordered dashboard card underneath. Tandem and Moa share the same green filled button. Pennywise's black filled button sits next to a text-link secondary. Every card uses labeled rows with right-aligned amounts, thin progress/segment bars, and a tinted callout box (green decision panel, mint transfer box, 'Nice — you're on track'). The gray reassurance line repeats. The headline type varies (centered serif, huge extended black, left-aligned Korean) but the layout skeleton is the same.

lost.text: Neither is weaker on direction: the two share an identical first screen and the same editorial serif plus ledger-table look built around Pennywise's left-to-spend budget, and the full pages differ only in pricing-table wording, where Y spells out "Not included" instead of a bare dash and names the plan in its button ("Try Plus free for 30 days"), which is why Y ships.

Neither version is weaker on direction: they share the same editorial serif, ledger-style budget table and plain black-and-white palette, and differ only in small pricing-table details. Y's bare dashes for features Basic lacks are less clear than X's explicit 'Not included'.

The two screenshots match except for the async-standups section, where X uses a generic stack of quoted lines and even puts quotation marks around names like "Priya Shah · Lisbon", while Y turns the updates into city-tagged cards with teal rules and an orange rule for the blocked one, carrying over the hero's time-zone timeline look.

In Y, the async-standups section loses X's row of teammate standup cards with their city labels and blocked-status accents, and turns them into a list of quoted names that copies the pain-point section above, so the page's main time-zone product artifact becomes generic text.

Both share the same passbook-ledger serif direction, but X breaks the '입출금·예적금' label onto two lines in the hero table and uses a generic '무료로 시작하기' CTA, while Y keeps the label on one line and uses a CTA specific to the product, '앱 받고 1분 만에 연결하기'.

Y uses a generic "무료로 시작하기" CTA instead of X's product-specific "앱 받고 1분 만에 연결하기", and its hero ledger wraps "입출금·예적금" onto two lines, which breaks the clean passbook-row rhythm the concept depends on.
X uses the same serif-and-ledger look, but its overspend nudge is just a red status line instead of a row you can act on ("Move $14"), so it shows less of what the product actually does.
Y squeezes the product's nudge into a cramped red status cell and drops the header CTA and trust line, so the ledger reads more like a generic table than a budgeting coach that suggests a next move.

X is missing a brand mark, and its timeline bars don't line up with their local times (Jonah's 07:40 update starts at 06). That weakens the page's one idea, mapping updates across time zones, which Y gets right and backs with the logo and the highlighted 'is blocked'.

Y drops the interlocking-rings logo mark and the orange 'is blocked' highlight, and its update bars no longer start at each teammate's posted local time, so the time-zone timeline feels more generic and less tied to Tandem's 'no 6am call' story.

Neither is weaker on direction: both use the same passbook-ledger concept, serif headline and monochrome table, so the gap is only in polish, where Y adds a header download button, a more specific call to action and a trust line, though its ledger runs past the first screen.

Y drops the MyData/no-fee trust line and the transfer and alert rows inside the ledger, so its bankbook gets more generic, though it frames the whole ledger neatly within the first screen, which X's cut-off table doesn't.

X shows a plain category table with no per-category progress bars, so the hero mockup reads like a generic spreadsheet rather than this app's own envelope-style budget view, and its "before November starts" headline contradicts the in-progress November budget shown right below it.

Y removes the per-category spend bars that made the hero's budget table read as a budgeting tool, so its type and palette could belong to any dark fintech; it also says 'before November starts' when the page shows it is already November, and a white band cuts off the bottom of the first screen.

X has the same navy, yellow and serif look, but it has no logo mark and its decision card has no 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' line or orange 'blocked' highlight, so less of it is tied to Tandem's async-decision story.

Y drops the interlocking-rings Tandem mark, the 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' decision line, the orange 'blocked' accent and the 'nobody has to be online at the same time' promise, and those were the details that tied the look to this async-collaboration brand, so it reads as a generic navy SaaS hero (it also loses the Sign in link and the customer trust strip).

Both versions share the same art direction: the heavy Korean display headline, the sage background, the red 0원 accent and the fee-comparison transfer card, so neither has weaker direction; Y is the better ship because it adds navigation and a reassurance line under the CTA, while X has no nav.

Neither is weaker: both use the same Moa layout, with the heavy display headline, the sage and vermilion palette, and the fee-comparison receipt card. Y drops the nav and the sign-up reassurance line, which costs usability but leaves the art direction unchanged.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (same MD5 hashes for the fold and full-page shots), so both have the same Tandem-specific direction, with a timezone-stamped async log, decision cards and navy-and-yellow serif branding.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (same checksums for both the fold and full-page shots), so they share the same Tandem-specific direction, built around the time-zone standup log, the decision record and the 'give your team its mornings back' framing.

Neither version has weaker direction: the fold screenshots are byte-identical and the full pages share the same deep-green, Pennywise-specific look, so the only difference is the Plus pricing button, where Y's 'Try Plus free for 30 days' says which plan the trial is for and X's 'Start 30-day free trial' does not.

Neither is weaker on direction, since the two pages are pixel-identical apart from the Plus pricing button, which says 'Try Plus free for 30 days' in X and 'Start 30-day free trial' in Y; X's label names the plan you're picking, so it reads a little clearer.

Neither is weaker: both carry the same Tandem-specific direction, with a timezone timeline of teammates' local-time updates, warm off-white and forest-green palette, and async-first copy, and the folds and full pages look identical.

I can't tell the two apart: the first-screen images are byte-identical, and the full pages look the same at review size, so neither has weaker direction (both keep the Tandem time-zone timeline, decision log and the 'mornings back' story).

Y swaps the large serif step numerals in the three-step section for small grey '1단계' labels, so the editorial serif voice that carries the hero and the balance figure fades out there and that section looks like a generic template.
X is otherwise the same page, but its three steps are small grey '1단계' captions instead of Y's large serif numerals that echo the headline type, so that part of the onboarding story feels generic.
X uses a generic budgeting-app headline with no link to the Pennywise name (Y ties it in with 'every penny'), so the look and copy would work just as well for any rival.

Y uses the generic headline 'A budgeting app that shows…' where X's 'every penny' line ties back to the Pennywise name, and Y drops the friendly 'Nice — you're on track' nudge, so its copy could belong to any rival; it also shows a '$1 , 420' formatting glitch and has no nav CTA.

X has the same time-zone timeline concept but no brand mark, with a plain wordmark and a flat 'Blocked' state, so less of the Tandem identity carries through and it could more easily be any async-tool template.

Y uses the same timeline concept but has no logo mark, keeps Mei's 'Blocked' status in plain text instead of the alert color, and cuts the customer proof line, so it reads as a more generic SaaS template.
Neither version has weaker direction: both use the same serif headline, monochrome asset card and stacked balance bar, and Y only adds a header rule and a small trust line under the buttons.

Neither version has weaker direction: both share the same restrained monochrome look with a serif headline and a ledger-style asset card, and Y only drops X's reassurance line under the buttons (no sign-up or monthly fee, one-minute account linking, MyData-based) and the header divider, which costs some trust and structure but does not change the art direction.

The art direction is the same in both: the same restrained black-and-white editorial serif look, the same ledger-style budget mock-up and the same copy, so neither is weaker; X just has rougher details, with a centered table that breaks the ledger's left-aligned reading line and a broken, wrapped 'Start free' button on the Basic pricing card.

Both share the same editorial serif, monochrome ledger look built around budgeting, so neither has weaker direction; Y adds defects, though: centered table labels misalign with their left-aligned headers and the 'Start free' button wraps awkwardly.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (same checksums for the fold and full-page shots), both showing the same Tandem page with a timezone-timeline hero and async-team storytelling.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (matching checksums for both fold and full), so they share the same Tandem-specific look of time-zone timelines, an async decision log and the 'nobody online at the same time' headline.

Neither version is weaker on direction: they share the same serif headline, deep-green fintech palette, product mockup and section layout, and differ only in the main button's label, where Y's '무료로 앱 받기' says exactly what happens next and matches the '앱 다운로드' nav button, while X's '무료로 시작하기' is vaguer.

Neither version has weaker direction: they share the same serif-led Korean headline, deep green palette and product-dashboard hero, and differ only in the primary CTA label, where Y's generic '무료로 시작하기' is less precise than X's '무료로 앱 받기', which matches the app-download action.

Neither is weaker: both use the same editorial serif and monochrome ledger look, so the only differences are polish, and Y wins there because its table and summary are left-aligned and easier to scan, despite redundant subhead copy that leaves 'hours.' alone on the last line.

Neither is weaker: both use the same editorial serif and monochrome ledger look tied to Pennywise's 'budget honest' idea, but Y centers the category names and the on-track note inside the table, which makes it slower to scan than X's left-aligned rows, even though Y's shorter subhead avoids X's one-word last line.
Y drops the green emphasis on "the same time", so its headline loses the brand-colour accent that ties it to Tandem's green, and its subhead just repeats the headline instead of adding anything.

Neither version has weaker direction: both use the same wide grotesk headline, the same green and the same product mock that tracks a spec across time zones; Y only adds green to part of the headline and cuts subcopy that repeats it, which tidies the page without changing its look.

Neither version has weaker direction: both share the same serif headline, deep-green palette and asset-dashboard mockup, and differ only in the CTA row, where Y's single primary button and trust line make for a clearer hierarchy.

Neither version has weaker direction: both share the same serif Korean headline, deep-green palette and live asset-dashboard mockup, and differ only in the CTA row (X has one primary button, a text link and a trust line; Y has App Store and Google Play buttons and shows more of the mockup).

X leaves its Zero-based budgets and Gentle nudges cards as empty colored tiles instead of mini product UI, so those cards lose the budgeting-specific feel. It also centers the dashboard tile text, which looks more like a generic template, and the stray capital 'Eating' in the headline is a polish error.

Y leaves out the product's own mini-interfaces: its Zero-based budgets and Gentle nudges cards are empty, its centered dashboard tiles look generic, and its headline has a stray capital in "Eating", so it reads less like Pennywise's actual app.

X drops the printed-receipt motif in the 'Also in the workspace' section and falls back to a generic two-column feature list, while Y presents it as an itemised receipt and gives the customer logos their own row, carrying the 'standup already printed' idea further down the page.

Y turns the 'Also in the workspace' itemised receipt into a plain two-column feature grid and shrinks the customer logos into a line of text, which weakens the printed-receipt idea that makes the page belong to Tandem.

X drops the receipt motif in its middle sections, so the transfer-fee and security bands fall back to generic white-band text lists, while Y carries the torn-paper fee receipt through the 0원 transfer section and an alternating steps layout.

Y drops the receipt for the 0원 transfer-fee section, so the page's key fee claim ends up as a plain white band of lists, and the receipt metaphor that makes the brand ownable starts to fade halfway down.

Y uses the same orange, lilac and black tile system, but its long, clumsy three-line headline pushes the budget tiles below the fold and crops them, so the page's most distinctive element, the live 'left to spend' dashboard, loses its impact.

Y uses the same orange, lilac and black card system, but its headline 'every dollar has a job' is a stock budgeting line any rival could use, and it drops X's '$14 over eating out' hook that ties the headline to the dashboard cards below.

Y swaps X's 'one digest for each person's morning' copy for a generic 'specs, decisions, roadmaps and standups live in one place' line and adds a stock AI-summaries teaser and logo strip, which weakens the printed-overnight-receipt idea that makes the page belong to Tandem.

Y drops the receipt motifs that carry past the hero card in X (the dashed perforation rule under the nav, the logo mark, the richer 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' detail), so the receipt idea sits only inside one card and not across the page.

X uses the receipt idea only for the hero card; Y also carries it into the dashed rule under the nav, the brand name in the headline and the 'like one receipt' section copy, and X's cramped, crooked stamp and missing trust line make it feel less finished.

Y uses the receipt idea less fully: it drops the dashed perforated rule under the nav and the monospace quantity columns, and its stamp is cramped and sits on top of the double rule, so it looks like a stuck-on badge instead of part of the receipt.
